pr_body:
# Add HttpContext.Endpoint property

Overview of the Problem
The goal was to introduce an Endpoint property directly on the HttpContext class. This change aims to make endpoint handling more intuitive and seamless, improving the developer experience by avoiding the need for extension methods like GetEndpoint and SetEndpoint.

## Description

Changes to the HttpContext Class
New Endpoint Property:
Justification: Adding Endpoint as a direct property on HttpContext allows for more straightforward access to the current endpoint associated with the request. This change enhances usability and aligns with the way other intrinsic properties (like Request, Response) are accessed.
Details: The Endpoint property uses the existing feature collection to fetch or initialize an IEndpointFeature instance, which stores the current endpoint.

Modifications to the DefaultHttpContext Class
Implementation of Endpoint Property:
Getter: Retrieves the Endpoint from the IEndpointFeature. If the feature doesn't exist, it initializes a new EndpointFeature instance.
Setter: Sets the Endpoint on the IEndpointFeature. If the endpoint is null, it resets the feature accordingly.
Justification: This approach maintains backward compatibility, as the existing feature mechanism is preserved. It ensures that endpoints are handled uniformly across different contexts and allows for easy future extensions.

Removal of the SetEndpoint Method from EndpointHttpContextExtensions
Justification: With the Endpoint property now directly on HttpContext, the SetEndpoint method in the EndpointHttpContextExtensions class became redundant. Removing it reduces code duplication and potential confusion.

Adjustments to Unit Tests
Updated Test Cases:
Justification: The test cases were modified to align with the new Endpoint property implementation. Previously, the tests relied on the SetEndpoint method, but now they test the direct interaction with the Endpoint property.
Details: The test ensuring that no IEndpointFeature is set on a context without a feature has been adjusted. Now, it verifies that an EndpointFeature is always created if accessed, even if the endpoint is set to null.

Any feedback would be appreciated

Fixes #50522

issue_context.title: Add HttpContext.Endpoint property
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe the problem.

ASP.NET Core includes the [GetEndpoint and SetEndpoint extension methods](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/00d0038f937f0059a847fde504649fe33ec935e0/src/Http/Http.Abstractions/src/Routing/EndpointHttpContextExtensions.cs#L13-L56) for working with endpoints and HttpContext.

I think endpoints have become such an intrinsic feature to ASP.NET Core that we should consider making it a real property on `HttpContext`. A property would be easier to use (no need to have the right namespace for the extension method) and feel better to use compared to a method.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add `HttpContext.Endpoint` property.

### Additional context

_No response_
comments:
While endpoints are a very intrinsic feature, I think only a very small percentage of the code referencing the `HttpContext` need it. `HttpContext.GetEndpoint()` and `SetEndpoint()` don't seem that hard to find.

> A property would be easier to use (no need to have the right namespace for the extension method) and feel better to use compared to a method.

I agree that the ergonomics of a property would be way nicer than the Javaesque get/set methods, but I don't think the namespace is a problem. It's included in the same namespace and assembly as `HttpContext` itself. `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http` is a default implicit using. And while it's possible to use `HttpContext` without using its namespace, I don't think it's very common.

The downsides are this would be the first virtual member on `HttpContext`, and the first member that returns a nullable value. Furthermore, you'd end up only getting an `Endpoint` when most people would probably prefer if it was typed as a `RouteEndpoint` so they can also inspect the `RoutePattern`, because that's what it's going to be 99.99% of the time it's not null.

This will also create some confusion over whether `GetEndpoint()` or `Endpoint` is preferred and whether or not they do the same thing unless we deprecate the extension methods. Generally, it's best to have only one obvious way to do things, but deprecating the extension methods creates unnecessary hassle for people maintaining existing code.

API Review Notes:

- `context.Endpoint?.DisplayName` is a lot nicer than `context.GetEndpoint()?.DisplayName` 
- Most people don't want the `RoutePattern`, they want the `EndpointMetadataCollection`
- It aligns the debug view for the `HttpContext` which includes the "Endpoint".
- We would support an info-level analyzer/fixer to use the new property over the extension method, but we do not want to obsolete the extension methods.
- Should it be on `HttpRequest` like `RouteValues` since it is determined based on the incoming `HttpRequest`?
  - This might be more confusing considering the extension method is already extending `HttpContext`.
- Would it be even more convenient to expose the `EndpointMetadataCollection` directly?
  - The metadata doesn't include a name so is less interesting in the debugger.
  - It would be weird to expose the metadata separately from the endpoint.
- The default implementation of the virtual should use the feature collection.

API Approved!

```diff
namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http;
 
public abstract class HttpContext
{
+     public virtual Endpoint? Endpoint { get; set; }
}
```

review_comments:
I think this is _technically_ a breaking behavioral change since the feature is set on the context even if there is no endpoint. This could pose an issue for codepaths that assumed that no `IEndpointFeature` == no endpoint. 

From looking at usages of this API ([ref](https://grep.app/search?current=2&q=.Get%3CIEndpointFeature%3E&filter[lang][0]=C%23)), this might not functionally be a problem but good to note.
Would it be worthwhile to confirm that `context.Endpoint` agrees?  Would it be worthwhile to try the same test with `context.Endpoint = null`, rather than `SetEndpoint`?
Do I understand correctly that this is expected to update the `IEndpointFeature` appropriately?

Yes, setting context.Endpoint = endpoint; will appropriately update the IEndpointFeature.Endpoint. The HttpContext.Endpoint property directly interacts with the IEndpointFeature, ensuring that any updates are synchronized between the two.
